text.p: Turkish central bank heavily funded banks with Friday value on Thursday in order to meet state banks' cash needs stemming from mid-month public sector salary payments and weekend demand, bankers said. It lent 24.1 trillion lira at 69 percent via tmrw/next and 24.7 trillion lira at 70 percent via tmrw/week. But it withdrew 4.2 trillion lira of idle cash at 52 percent on overnight towards the close.
Bankers said excess liquidity remained in the market probably because some banks had late cash inflows.

The rise in average overnight money rate was a minor 0.53 percentage points to 68.57 percent because of the central bank's late deal at 52 percent although the rates mostly remained at around 70-71 percent during the day.
But the average overnight repo rate jumped to 73.22 percent from Wednesday's 70.35 percent on tight liquidity although paper supply decreased in the bond market, bankers said.
They said paper demand firmed because of the imbalanced distribution of banks' paper portfolios and bond sales in the recent auctions remaining below the redemption amounts.

Bond yields rose to around 104 percent level from previous 103 percent on selling, but volume was again very thin due to mounting political uncertainty. The most active one was April 22,1998 which yielded 104.34 percent, up 1.32 percentage points from Wednesday.
The Turkish lira eased to 144,070 against the dollar from Wednesday's close of 143,550 in line with dollar/mark.
